solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Retiring, English commoner grabs the main cheese

indicators.note: retiring means drawing back, so the whole built string is read backwards
the commoner grabbing something holds it inside

parts.note: a pleb is an ordinary commoner, from plebeian
the main is a poetic name for the open sea

explanation.surface: A modest English peasant, shy and withdrawing, snatches a cheese of great importance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the main' is the poetic name for the sea; 'Retiring' reverses the whole assembled string, giving ESEAPLEB backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Bel Paese is a mild, soft Italian cow's-milk variety sold in foil-wrapped rounds.

clue.text: British with hats going outside start to need sun-block?

indicators.note: the hats go round the outside of the next piece, enclosing it

parts.note: lids is slang for hats

indicators.note: the start to a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: Britons in hats, heading out, first think of needing sunscreen.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a playful definition: window shades literally block the sun.
explanation.definitionFit: Window shades pulled down keep out sunlight, so they are a sun-block in a literal sense.

clue.text: Extremists in lowlands lie about Democrat victory

parts.note: the outermost letters of lowlands are L and S, written out with the joining word spelt in full

indicators.note: the word lie goes about, surrounding, the next piece

parts.note: taken as written
D is the abbreviation for a US Democrat

explanation.surface: Radicals in low-lying country spread falsehoods about the Democratic Party's win.
explanation.walkthrough: The extremes of lowlands are written as a phrase, L-AND-S, giving five letters rather than two.
explanation.definitionFit: An overwhelming electoral win is called by this name, after a collapse of earth that sweeps all before it.

clue.text: Training pilots cease to have lodging nearby

parts.note: the ATC, Air Training Corps, is a British cadet organisation teaching young people to fly
to lose something is to cease to have it
quarters are lodgings or accommodation

explanation.surface: Trainee aviators must give up their billets close by.
explanation.walkthrough: The ATC is Britain's Air Training Corps, a youth organisation sponsored by the RAF.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means very near to someone or something, in close proximity.

clue.text: Organist endlessly amazed lady in Milan

indicators.note: amazed suggests being thrown into confusion, so the letters are jumbled
endlessly means without its final letter

explanation.surface: A church musician left a woman in Milan endlessly astonished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' drops the last letter of Organist, leaving ORGANIS, and 'amazed' rearranges it.
explanation.definitionFit: Italian title or form of address for a married woman, equivalent to Mrs or madam.

clue.text: Cavaliers primarily hunt a couple of Roundheads in diocese retreating

indicators.note: primarily points to the first letter of the word hunt
the pair of letters sits within the turned-round bishopric
retreating means going backwards, so the word is reversed

parts.note: a see is a bishop's diocese

indicators.note: a couple of letters means the opening two of the word

explanation.surface: A Civil War tale: Royalists chase down Parliamentarians who are falling back through a bishop's territory.
explanation.walkthrough: SEE reversed by 'retreating' gives EES, which takes in RO from 'a couple of Roundheads'. Cavaliers and Roundheads were the opposing sides in the English Civil War.
explanation.definitionFit: Cavaliers in the sense of gallant, chivalrous men are brave champions.

clue.text: Hollywood actress given lily flower, large and golden

parts.note: Lily is a pet form of the given name Elizabeth
a flower is something that flows, a river; the Tay is a Scottish river
or is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: A film star is presented with a big, golden lily bloom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flower' means a river, here the Tay in Scotland; 'given' and 'lily' hide a first name, since Lily is short for Elizabeth.
explanation.definitionFit: Star of Cleopatra and Cat on a Hot Tin Roof, among the great film beauties of Hollywood.

clue.text: Musicians etc raised in middle of Bootle

indicators.note: the turned word sits inside the central letters
the middle of a six-letter word is its central pair of letters
raised in a down clue means read upwards, so the word is reversed

explanation.surface: Musicians and so on were brought up in the heart of a Merseyside town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' reverses etc, as a down clue reads upwards. Bootle is a town near Liverpool.
explanation.definitionFit: A group of eight players or singers performing together forms an ensemble of this size.

clue.text: Son at bay on the rocks

parts.note: an animal at bay is cornered, unable to escape

explanation.surface: A boy stranded in a bay, his boat wrecked on the rocks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the rocks' is not a shipwreck but slang for being short of money.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are informal ways of saying someone is short of money, in financial trouble.

clue.text: Before crumble, perhaps banger and veg

indicators.note: before places this piece ahead of the next one

parts.note: a banger is a battered old motor, an example of a car, hence perhaps
to rot is to decay or crumble away

explanation.surface: A British menu: before the crumble pudding, sausage and vegetables.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crumble' and 'banger' look like pudding and sausage, British dishes; here a banger is a clapped-out car.
explanation.definitionFit: An orange root vegetable, a familiar example of the class of food known as veg.

clue.text: Superhuman removing entrance for Greek school

indicators.note: removing the entrance means dropping the opening letter

parts.note: bionic describes superhuman powers given by electronic body parts

explanation.surface: A superhero quits the front door to attend a school in Greece.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing the first letter of BIONIC leaves the five-letter word.
explanation.definitionFit: The early philosophers of Ionia, such as Thales, formed a named school of Greek thought.

clue.text: One scrapped good heating equipment, changing hands initially

indicators.note: the opening letter, R for right hand, is switched for L, the left hand

parts.note: a radiator is a piece of heating equipment

explanation.surface: Someone threw out a perfectly good heater after it passed between owners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scrapped' looks like discarded but means fought. R and L stand for right and left, so swapping hands turns the opening R into L.
explanation.definitionFit: A Roman arena fighter scrapped, in the sense of fought, for a living and for show.

clue.text: Charged within sixty minutes after policeman's reproach

indicators.note: after places the following piece behind the first

parts.note: a DI is a detective inspector; with the possessive the piece is DIS

indicators.note: within means one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: sixty minutes make an hour
a circuit that is charged or live is on

explanation.surface: A police officer's rebuke after someone is charged inside the hour.
explanation.walkthrough: DI is a detective inspector, a British police rank.
explanation.definitionFit: A noun meaning disgrace or shame, something that brings reproach on a person.

clue.text: Current sheep behave badly

parts.note: AC is alternating current
a tup is a ram, a male sheep

explanation.surface: Present-day sheep are misbehaving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Current' looks like up-to-date but means electric current.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom for misbehaving or showing off, or a machine malfunctioning.

clue.text: Name Nick, when handing over some pictures

indicators.note: handing over suggests turning something over, so the letters are read backwards
some means only part of the words is taken

explanation.surface: Give your name, Nick, when passing across a few photographs.
explanation.walkthrough: AMENIC sits inside 'Name Nick'; 'handing over' turns it round. 'The pictures' is an old name for the movies.
explanation.definitionFit: Going to the pictures is a British way of saying going to the movies, so the word names the film house.

clue.text: Sentimentality Malcolm regularly displayed during date perhaps

indicators.note: during places one piece within the span of the other

parts.note: a date palm is an example of a tree

indicators.note: regularly means every other letter of the name

explanation.surface: Malcolm keeps showing mushy feelings, perhaps on a romantic outing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'date' looks like a romantic evening but is the date palm, an example of a tree; 'regularly' takes the even letters of Malcolm.
explanation.definitionFit: Cloying, sugary sentiment is figuratively called by the name of a thick syrup.

clue.text: Plant pot reduced, as mimosa unopened sadly

indicators.note: reduced means cut short by its final letter

parts.note: a crock is an earthenware pot

indicators.note: sadly signals the letters are in a sorry, disordered state
unopened means without its first letter

explanation.surface: A gardener laments a shrunken pot, with the mimosa still in tight bud.
explanation.walkthrough: CROC is CROCK cut short; 'unopened' leaves IMOSA, which 'sadly' rearranges into OSMIA.
explanation.definitionFit: A cormous garden plant of the iris family, also called montbretia, with arching orange-red flower spikes.

clue.text: Excess fat attracts rooks and one other type of bird

indicators.note: attracts means draws the next pieces into it

parts.note: podge is excess body fat
R is the chess abbreviation for a rook, so two give RR
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Plenty of fat draws rooks and another kind of bird to the feeder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bird' here is British slang for a prison sentence, the type that is not feathered.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for time served in prison, an alternative to bird, which also means a jail term.

clue.text: Runner describes very briefly why injury may occur

indicators.note: describes means draws a line round, enclosing the next piece

parts.note: a runner is a river; the Ouse is an English river

indicators.note: briefly means cut short by the last letter

explanation.surface: An athlete gives a short account of how the injury happened.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Runner' is a river, the Ouse, which goes around VER; 'describes' is used in the geometry sense of tracing round.
explanation.definitionFit: Excessive repetitive use of a joint or muscle is a common cause of strain.

clue.text: Money pencilled in European leader's to raise in relief?

indicators.note: pencilled in means written provisionally into the gap

parts.note: a boss is a leader; the possessive adds no letter

explanation.surface: Cash is tentatively written into a European chief's budget to give relief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'relief' suggests aid, but it is the raised surface of a design.
explanation.definitionFit: To stamp or carve a design so it stands out from the surface is to work it in relief.

clue.text: Where one teaches some bass?

definitions.meaning: a place of education where a teacher works
a group of fish such as bass swimming together

explanation.definitionFit: A teaching establishment, and also a shoal of fish; bass are a kind of fish.

clue.text: Slight wound from constant rogue in school

indicators.note: the pieces go inside the abbreviation for school

parts.note: C is the symbol for a constant, such as the speed of light
a rat is a rogue or treacherous person

explanation.surface: A minor injury picked up from a persistent bully at school.
explanation.definitionFit: A shallow mark on the skin made by something sharp is a minor injury.

clue.text: Find new accommodation for fellow back in capital

indicators.note: in places the turned piece inside the city

parts.note: Rome is the Italian capital

indicators.note: back means the word is read backwards

parts.note: he refers to a male fellow

explanation.surface: Relocating a man back in the capital city.
explanation.definitionFit: To place a pet or person in a different household is to give them a new home.

clue.text: One regrets keeping close to criminal overlord

indicators.note: keeping means holding the next piece inside

parts.note: a ruer is one who rues, who regrets

indicators.note: the close to a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: Someone full of regret stays near a criminal mastermind.
explanation.definitionFit: A sovereign or person in supreme command over others.

clue.text: Cosmetic business heading for recovery

parts.note: a line is a line of business, a trade

indicators.note: the heading for a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A beauty company is on its way back to health.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyeliner or lip liner is a make-up product for outlining features.

clue.text: Woman contributes to unadorned song

indicators.note: she contributes to the word by entering it

parts.note: bare means plain, unadorned
Carol is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A woman adds her voice to a plain, simple tune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Woman' and 'song' tempt CAROL as the answer; here she is only the filling.
explanation.definitionFit: A Venetian gondolier's song, or a piece of music imitating its rocking rhythm.

clue.text: Daughter playing tennis limits her familiar service

indicators.note: the rearranged word limits, bounding on each side, the next piece
playing suggests the letters at play, rearranged

parts.note: in familiar speech her is dropped to 'er

explanation.surface: A girl at tennis keeps her serve within bounds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'playing' rearranges tennis into INNSET, split round ER, the dropped-h form of her. 'service' means crockery, not a tennis serve.
explanation.definitionFit: A matching set of plates and dishes for a meal is called a dinner service.

clue.text: One's unsure in this dance

definitions.meaning: a state of uncertainty or waiting in which one is left undecided
a Caribbean dance passing under a lowered bar

explanation.definitionFit: Both a state of uncertain suspension and a West Indian bending-backwards dance under a bar.

clue.text: Everything vacated on ship's departure

indicators.note: vacated means emptied, leaving only the outer letters

parts.note: re means on, concerning
SS is steamship; the possessive adds no letter

explanation.surface: Everything was cleared out on the ship before it left.
explanation.definitionFit: The act of going out or leaving a place, a formal synonym for an exit.

clue.text: Irish Lord backed into the elderly group

indicators.note: into places the pieces inside the following word
backed means read backwards

parts.note: gad is an old minced oath for God, the Lord

explanation.surface: An Irish peer retreated into a band of senior citizens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backed' turns GAD into DAG; IRDAG goes into THE.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names the period of active retirement after working life, and so older people as a group.
